mathAndIncentives.counterexamples: All four calculations check: 1-.25/.30=+16.6667% and 1-.25/.25=0; 1-.9025/.40=-125.625% and 1-.9025/.25=-261%; 1-200/20=-900%; 1-.19/.20=+5%, 1-.19/.25=+24%, and 1-19/20=+5%. The stated band and component-floor results follow from the table, with exact-boundary assignment defined.
mathAndIncentives.properScores: Binary Brier and unordered categorical Brier/2 are proper for their declared exhaustive event spaces. The central 90% interval score width + 20 times each outside-endpoint distance is proper for the frozen 5th and 95th margin quantiles. The grade bands and D cap are editorial summaries, not themselves proper scoring rules. Publishing raw paired losses is essential.
mathAndIncentives.uniformCap: A zero or negative skill against uniform capping winner/overall at D is mathematically coherent and prevents a 50/50 forecast from earning B solely because the history baseline was worse. It can cap an otherwise A margin model at D, so keep the margin subgrade plainly visible and describe D as lack of useful pair/group discrimination in this cycle, not proof of long-run miscalibration. Do not give 50/50 a separate no-call penalty.
mathAndIncentives.intervalIncentive: A full [-100,+100] percentage-point interval has width 200 and 100% coverage on the legal margin range but interval score 200; the example's -900% skill versus score 20 is correct. Avoid a second coverage-only grade. An authenticated same-target history interval is still prerequisite.

materialRevisionsBeforeLock.evidence: The currently saved 435-race House polling result has outcome-party sets: 226 D/R, 191 D/R/O, 13 D only, 4 D/O, 1 R only. Thus 'the frozen listed D/R/Other outcomes are exhaustive' and uniform 1/K as if every listed set covers every possible official winner are not established. A single-category K=1 uniform reference assigns probability 1 to that listed group and says nothing about an unmodeled official winner.
materialRevisionsBeforeLock.change: Before results, name the actual House grading event and support. If grading official winner party D/R/O, owner must approve a scoring mapping that always has those three categories, maps every official winner (including unmodeled write-ins/independents) to one, and explicitly explains any zero-probability completion for categories missing from a native conditional forecast; use uniform 1/3 on that same three-category target. If native probabilities cannot honestly be read as full-field party probabilities, grade the declared conditional listed-outcome target with uniform 1/K on that exact support and add a separately precommitted scope-failure consequence (for example overall F) if an outside candidate wins. Do not quietly discard the race or call the conditional Brier full-field skill.

materialRevisionsBeforeLock.evidence: The refreshed Senate standard law forecasts first versus second named principal contender conditional pair share/winner proxy, not every possible seat winner. It has no all-candidate winner law.
materialRevisionsBeforeLock.change: Call the graded binary target 'which named contender leads the other under the locked final pair-vote/round rule' or 'principal-pair lead,' not an unqualified Senate winner. The 50/50 uniform comparator is exhaustive for this binary relative event. If a third candidate wins the seat but both named contenders have comparable official final votes, still score their relative pair lead and pair margin; separately display that the seat winner was outside support. Mark the pair target unavailable only when the locked vote/round/denominator cannot actually be reconstructed. Never force an outside seat winner into one principal category.

materialRevisionsBeforeLock.evidence: The 100% final-result gate prevents post-result cherry-picking, but one unavailable official round, missing candidate mapping, or indefinite recount can suppress every chamber letter. The phrase 'unsupported' can otherwise become a post-outcome escape hatch.
materialRevisionsBeforeLock.change: Freeze event, fallback official source, certification/finality rule, and explicit escalation/review dates before returns. Keep every locked row in N; only pre-outcome-declared structurally unavailable pair margins are outside their separate margin cohort. An outside-support observed winner triggers the precommitted support-failure consequence rather than a removable exclusion. For genuinely unresolved results, optionally publish a letter early only if exhaustive best/worst admissible completions of those rows leave the same component bands, uniform cap and overall floor; otherwise show raw n/N and 'letter pending' with named rows. This invariant-letter option preserves the fixed table without choosing an easy observed subset.

recommendedTableDisposition: Keep the proposed A >= +20%, B [+10%,+20%), C [0%,+10%), D [-10%,0%), F < -10% relative-skill bands as an explicit pre-outcome editorial choice, not an empirically established universal scale. Keep the lower-of-winner-and-interval component rule and the uniform SU<=0 D cap if the public page always displays raw Brier/interval scores, history and uniform references, component letters, cohort n/N and this cycle-specific meaning. The 2026 history comparator must be same-target and information-cutoff matched; the existing October 20 fundamentals edition is not automatically an October 26 baseline. Publish the signed table and target/support/missing-result rule before inspecting outcomes for grades.
additionalPrecision: Skill ratios require strictly positive matched baseline mean loss; when zero, publish raw paired differences and withhold that component letter under the precommitted rule.

For 35 correlated Senate races and one cycle, relative-skill cutoffs can swing with a small baseline loss. A letter describes the locked cycle only; it is not a statistical confidence statement or model calibration certificate.

Interval score is proper for the two stated quantiles but does not score the entire margin CDF. This is acceptable if the public label says '90% interval skill,' not full distribution skill. The sidecar's model-implied expected error/coverage is not an observed score or grade.
checksNotPerformed: No 2026 outcomes were used, no grade calculated, and no product or native files were modified.

houseOwnerDecisionReportedByRoot.decision: Evaluate House official party winner on fixed exhaustive D/R/O categories. Native missing groups receive zero probability in the predeclared scoring mapping; uniform categorical reference is 1/3 for all 435 contests. An observed winner outside a listed modeled group remains in the 435-row ordinary Brier or Brier/2 score and receives an infinite un-clipped log loss if log loss is displayed. Keep a separate omitted candidate-ID diagnostic. Native forecast probabilities and files remain unchanged.
houseOwnerDecisionReportedByRoot.interpretiveCaveat: A (.5,.5,0) D/R/O forecast beats uniform thirds when D or R wins because it excludes O; this is information about Other exclusion, not proof that it discriminates D from R. The SU<=0 D cap therefore is not an all-50/50 D/R detector under this House reference. Show raw scores and this distinction.
